chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Fudayl from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said:

I asked him about a man who killed a pigeon from the pigeons of the Sanctuary (Haram) while he was not in a state of Ihram. He said: Upon him is its value, which is one dirham, which he gives as charity or uses to buy food for the pigeons of the Sanctuary. And if he killed it while he was in Ihram in the Sanctuary, then upon him is a sheep and the value of the pigeon. And that which also indicates that whenever he slaughtered it in the Sanctuary while he was Muhrim (not in Ihram), it did not obligate him more than the value.

key_terms.مُحِلٌّ: One who is not in Ihram (free from restrictions)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of Ihram (pilgrimal consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for killing a pigeon in the Haram if one is in Ihram versus not in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar establishes the specific financial compensation (qimah) for killing a sanctuary pigeon, distinguishing between the liability of a non-pilgrim (one dirham) and a pilgrim in Ihram (a sheep plus the value). It highlights the sanctity of the Haram's wildlife and the increased spiritual weight of violations during Hajj, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on precise monetary valuation for minor animals. The ruling underscores the principle that while the act is a sin, the primary remedy is restorative justice through charity or consumption, rather than corporal punishment.
